title.zh: 卷二百〇二 志第一百五十五 藝文一
title.raw: 卷二百〇二 志第一百五十五 藝文一 Volume 202 Treatises 155: Arts and Literature 1

sentences.zh: 藝文一 《易》曰：“觀乎天文，以察時變；

translations.literal: Arts and Literature 1. The 《Changes》 says: "Observe the patterns of heaven to discern the changes of the seasons;
translations.idiomatic: Arts and Literature 1. The Book of Changes says: "Look to the patterns of heaven to read the turning of the seasons;

translations.literal: observe the patterns of human culture to transform and complete the world."
translations.idiomatic: observe the patterns of human affairs to civilize and perfect the realm."

translations.literal: That culture bears upon the fortunes of the age has long been understood.
translations.idiomatic: That writing and culture matter to the rise and fall of an age has been clear for a very long time.

sentences.zh: 然書契以來，文字多而世代日降；

translations.literal: Yet since the invention of writing, though texts have multiplied, successive ages have daily declined;
translations.idiomatic: Yet from the time writing was invented, although texts grew ever more numerous, each generation seemed to decline further;

sentences.zh: 秦火而後，文字多而世教日興，其故何哉？

translations.literal: while after the Qin burning, though texts have multiplied, civilizing instruction has daily flourished—why is this?
translations.idiomatic: yet after the Qin bibliocaust, although texts again multiplied, moral instruction in the world rose day by day—what is the reason?

sentences.zh: 蓋世道升降，人心習俗之致然，非徒文字之所為也。

translations.literal: Surely it is because the rise and fall of the age's way and the habits of people's hearts and customs make it so—not the work of writing alone.
translations.idiomatic: It is surely because the ascent or descent of the age and the drift of popular hearts and customs bring this about—not writing by itself.

sentences.zh: 然去古既遠，苟無斯文以範防之，則愈趨而愈下矣。

translations.literal: Yet as one grows distant from antiquity, if this culture is not used to fence and guard against decline, then one trends ever further downward.
translations.idiomatic: But once antiquity lies far behind, unless this literary culture is used as a barrier and safeguard, society only slides further down.

sentences.zh: 故由秦而降，每以斯文之盛衰，占斯世之治忽焉。

translations.literal: Therefore from the Qin downward, people have regularly gauged whether an age is well governed or neglected by whether this culture flourishes or fails.
translations.idiomatic: Hence from the Qin dynasty onward, each age has been read by whether literary culture waxed or waned—by that sign one judged order or disorder.

sentences.zh: 宋有天下，先後三百餘年，考其治化之汙隆，風氣之離合，雖不足以擬倫三代，然其時君汲汲於道藝，輔治之臣莫不以經術為先務，學士搢紳先生，談道德性命之學，不絕於口，豈不彬彬乎進於周之文哉！

translations.literal: The Song possessed the realm for more than three hundred years in all; examining the rise and fall of its governance and the convergence or divergence of its customs, though it cannot fully match the Three Dynasties, yet its rulers were urgently devoted to the Way and the arts, ministers assisting governance all took classical learning as their first task, and scholars, gentry, and teachers spoke of the learning of moral nature without cease—was this not a flourishing advance toward the culture of Zhou!
translations.idiomatic: The Song held the empire for over three centuries; weighing the ebb and flow of its rule and the unity or fracture of its mores, it may not equal the Three Dynasties, yet its emperors pressed hard after the Way and the arts, every minister who aided rule put the classics first, and literati, officials, and masters never ceased discussing the philosophy of nature and principle—was this not a cultured advance toward the brilliance of Zhou!

sentences.zh: 宋之不競，或以為文勝之弊，遂歸咎焉，此以功利為言，未必知道者之論也。

translations.literal: That the Song could not compete, some attribute to the defect of cultural excess and blame it accordingly—this is talk in terms of utility and profit, not necessarily the view of one who knows the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Some say the Song lost its edge because culture grew too strong and blame literature for it—but that is the language of profit and utility, not necessarily the judgment of one who understands the Way.

sentences.zh: 曆代之書籍，莫厄於秦，莫富於隋、唐。

translations.literal: Of books through the ages, none suffered calamity like those in the Qin, and none were richer than those of Sui and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Books of successive dynasties met no disaster like the Qin burning, and no hoard like those of Sui and Tang.

sentences.zh: 隋嘉則殿書三十七萬卷。

translations.literal: In the Jiade Hall of Sui there were 370,000 juan of books.
translations.idiomatic: Sui's Hall of Accumulated Virtue held 370,000 juan.

sentences.zh: 而唐之藏書，開元最盛，為卷八萬有奇。

translations.literal: Among Tang collections, the Kaiyuan period was richest, with somewhat more than 80,000 juan.
translations.idiomatic: Tang imperial collections peaked under Kaiyuan at a little over 80,000 juan.

sentences.zh: 其間唐人所自為書，幾三萬卷，則舊書之傳者，至是蓋亦鮮矣。

translations.literal: Of these, books composed by Tang authors themselves were nearly 30,000 juan, so of older books transmitted, by then very few remained.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly 30,000 juan were works Tang authors wrote themselves, so of older texts still handed down, few indeed survived by then.

sentences.zh: 陵遲逮於五季，幹戈相尋，海寓鼎沸，斯民不復見《詩》、《書》、《禮》、《樂》之化。

translations.literal: Decline reached the Five Dynasties; arms followed one upon another, the realm seethed like a cauldron, and the people no longer saw the transforming influence of the 《Odes》, 《Documents》, 《Rites》, and 《Music》.
translations.idiomatic: Decay ran on into the Five Dynasties: war followed war, the empire boiled, and the people no longer knew the civilizing power of the Odes, Documents, Rites, and Music.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，始有經籍刻板，學者無筆劄之勞，獲睹古人全書。

translations.literal: In the Xiande era of Zhou, block printing of the classics first appeared; scholars were spared the labor of copying by hand and could see the ancients' complete books.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Zhou's Xiande reign, classics were first cut on blocks; scholars no longer had to copy by hand and could read whole ancient books.

sentences.zh: 然亂離以來，編帙散佚，幸而存者，百無二三。

translations.literal: Yet since the turmoil, bindings were scattered and lost; of what by fortune survived, not two or three in a hundred remained.
translations.idiomatic: But since the chaos, codices had scattered and vanished; of what still existed, scarcely two or three in a hundred.

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song there were somewhat more than 10,000 juan of books.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song there were a little over ten thousand juan.

sentences.zh: 其後削平諸國，收其圖籍，及下詔遣使購求散亡，三館之書，稍復增益。

translations.literal: Afterward, as the various states were pacified, their maps and registers were collected, and edicts were issued sending envoys to purchase what had been scattered and lost; the books of the Three Institutes gradually increased again.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the rival states were subdued, their maps and libraries were taken in; edicts sent envoys to buy up what had been lost, and the Three Institutes' holdings slowly grew again.

sentences.zh: 太宗始於左升龍門北建崇文院，而徙三館之書以實之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong first built the Chongwen Court north of the Left Ascending Dragon Gate and moved the books of the Three Institutes to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong first built the Chongwen Court north of the Left Ascending Dragon Gate and moved the Three Institutes' books there to stock it.

sentences.zh: 又分三館書萬餘卷，別為書庫，目曰“秘閣”。

translations.literal: He also separated out more than 10,000 juan from the Three Institutes' holdings into another book repository called the "Secret Repository."
translations.idiomatic: He also set aside more than ten thousand juan from the Three Institutes into a separate library called the Secret Repository.

sentences.zh: 閣成，親臨幸觀書，賜從臣及直館宴。

translations.literal: When the repository was completed, he personally visited to view the books and granted banquets to attending ministers and those on duty in the institutes.
translations.idiomatic: When it was finished, he visited in person to read, and feasted his ministers and institute staff.

sentences.zh: 又命近習侍衛之臣縱觀群書。

translations.literal: He also ordered close attendants and guards to browse the books freely.
translations.idiomatic: He also commanded personal attendants and guards to roam freely among the collections.

sentences.zh: 真宗時，命三館寫四部書二本，置禁中之龍圖閣及後苑之太清樓，而玉宸殿、四門殿亦各有書萬餘卷。

translations.literal: In the Zhenzong period he ordered the Three Institutes to copy the books of the four categories in duplicate sets, placing them in the Dragon Diagram Hall within the Forbidden City and in the Great Clarity Tower in the rear park; the Jade Hall and the Hall of the Four Gates each also had more than 10,000 juan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenzong the Three Institutes copied the four categories in two sets each, one for the Dragon Diagram Pavilion in the palace and one for the Great Clarity Tower in the rear garden; the Jade Hall and Four Gates Hall each held over ten thousand juan as well.

sentences.zh: 又以秘閣地隘，分內藏西庫以廣之，其右文之意，亦雲至矣。

translations.literal: Because the Secret Repository site was cramped, part of the inner storehouse's west depot was divided off to enlarge it; his intent to honor culture reached its utmost.
translations.idiomatic: The Secret Repository grounds were cramped, so part of the inner treasury's west store was opened to expand it—his esteem for letters could hardly go further.

sentences.zh: 已而王宮火，延及崇文、秘閣，書多煨燼。

translations.literal: Before long a fire in the royal palace spread to the Chongwen Court and Secret Repository, and many books were reduced to ashes.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a fire in the royal palace reached the Chongwen Court and Secret Repository, and many books were burned to ash.

sentences.zh: 其僅存者，遷於右掖門外，謂之崇文外院，命重寫書籍，選官詳覆校勘，常以參知政事一人領之，書成，歸於太清樓。

translations.literal: What barely survived was moved outside the Right Arm Gate, called the Outer Chongwen Court; he ordered books rewritten, officials chosen to review and collate carefully, with one Vice Grand Councillor regularly in charge; when copying was done, books returned to the Great Clarity Tower.
translations.idiomatic: What little remained was moved outside the Right Arm Gate as the Outer Chongwen Court; he ordered books recopied and officials chosen for careful collation, usually led by one Vice Grand Councillor; finished copies went back to the Great Clarity Tower.

sentences.zh: 仁宗既新作崇文院，命翰林學士張觀等編四庫書，仿《開元四部録》為《崇文總目》，書凡三萬六百六十九卷。

translations.literal: After Emperor Renzong rebuilt the Chongwen Court, he ordered Hanlin Academician Zhang Guan and others to compile the books of the four repositories, modeling the 《Comprehensive Catalogue of the Chongwen Court》 on the 《Kaiyuan Catalogue of the Four Categories》; books totaled 30,669 juan.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong rebuilt the Chongwen Court and had Hanlin academician Zhang Guan and others compile the four repositories, following the Kaiyuan Four-Category Catalogue to produce the Comprehensive Catalogue of the Chongwen Court—30,669 juan in all.

sentences.zh: 神宗改官制，遂廢館職，以崇文院為秘書省，秘閣經籍圖書以秘書郎主之，編輯校定，正其脫誤，則主於校書郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong reformed the official system, abolished institute posts, made the Chongwen Court the Secretariat, had Secretariat Gentlemen take charge of the Secret Repository's classics, maps, and books, and had Collators take charge of editing, collating, and correcting omissions and errors.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong reformed offices, abolished institute posts, made the Chongwen Court the Secretariat, put Secretariat Gentlemen over the Secret Repository's classics and maps, and Collators over editing, collation, and correction of errors.

sentences.zh: 徽宗時，更《崇文總目》之號為《秘書總目》。

translations.literal: In the Huizong period the title of the 《Comprehensive Catalogue of the Chongwen Court》 was changed to the 《Comprehensive Secretariat Catalogue》.
translations.idiomatic: Under Huizong the Comprehensive Catalogue of the Chongwen Court was renamed the Comprehensive Secretariat Catalogue.

sentences.zh: 詔購求士民藏書，其有所秘未見之書足備觀采者，仍命以官。

translations.literal: An edict sought books held by scholars and commoners; those with rare unseen books sufficient for imperial perusal were still granted office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict purchased books from private collections; owners of rare unseen works fit for the court still received official appointment.

sentences.zh: 且以三館書多逸遺，命建局以補全校正為名，設官總理，募工繕寫。

translations.literal: Because many books in the Three Institutes were missing, he ordered establishment of an office named for supplementing and collating the full collection, with officials to oversee it and workers hired to copy.
translations.idiomatic: Many Three Institutes books were lost, so he set up a bureau for full supplementation and collation, with supervising officials and hired copyists.

sentences.zh: 一置宣和殿，一置太清樓，一置秘閣。

translations.literal: One set was placed in the Xuanhe Hall, one in the Great Clarity Tower, and one in the Secret Repository.
translations.idiomatic: One copy went to the Xuanhe Hall, one to the Great Clarity Tower, one to the Secret Repository.

sentences.zh: 自熙寧以來，搜訪補輯，至是為盛矣。

translations.literal: From the Xining period onward, search and supplementation had been pursued; by then it reached its height.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xining, search and repair had continued; by then the collection was at its fullest.

sentences.zh: 嚐曆考之，始太祖、太宗、真宗三朝，三千三百二十七部，三萬九千一百四十二卷。

translations.literal: I have examined the records: first, the three reigns of Taizu, Taizong, and Zhenzong—3,327 titles, 39,142 juan.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing the registers: first the three reigns of Taizu, Taizong, and Zhenzong—3,327 titles in 39,142 juan.

sentences.zh: 次仁、英兩朝，一千四百七十二部，八千四百四十六卷。

translations.literal: Next the two reigns of Renzong and Yingzong—1,472 titles, 8,446 juan.
translations.idiomatic: Next Renzong and Yingzong—1,472 titles, 8,446 juan.

sentences.zh: 次神、哲、徽、欽四朝，一千九百六部，二萬六千二百八十九卷。

translations.literal: Next the four reigns of Shenzong, Zhezong, Huizong, and Qinzong—1,906 titles, 26,289 juan.
translations.idiomatic: Next Shenzong, Zhezong, Huizong, and Qinzong—1,906 titles, 26,289 juan.

sentences.zh: 三朝所録，則兩朝不復登載，而録其所未有者。

translations.literal: What the three reigns recorded was not entered again for the two reigns; only what they did not yet have was recorded.
translations.idiomatic: What the three earlier reigns listed was not repeated for the two later ones; only new acquisitions were entered.

translations.literal: The four reigns treated the two reigns the same way.
translations.idiomatic: The four-reign register did the same with the two-reign one.

sentences.zh: 最其當時之目，為部六千七百有五，為卷七萬三千八百七十有七焉。

translations.literal: At the fullest count of that time there were 6,705 titles and 73,877 juan.
translations.idiomatic: At the peak count of that era there were 6,705 titles and 73,877 juan.

sentences.zh: 迨夫靖康之難，而宣和、館閣之儲蕩然靡遺。

translations.literal: When the Jingkang disaster came, the stores of the Xuanhe period and the institutes were utterly swept away.
translations.idiomatic: Then came the disaster of Jingkang, and the Xuanhe and institute holdings were utterly lost.

sentences.zh: 高宗移蹕臨安，乃建秘書省於國史院之右，搜訪遺闕，屢優獻書之賞，於是四方之藏，稍稍復出，而館閣編輯，日益以富矣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong moved the court to Lin'an, he built the Secretariat to the right of the National History Institute, searched out what was missing, repeatedly offered rich rewards for presenting books, and so collections from the four directions gradually reappeared while institute editing grew daily richer.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong moved the court to Lin'an, built the Secretariat east of the National History Institute, sought lost works, repeatedly rewarded book donors, and collections from all quarters slowly returned while institute holdings grew richer by the day.

sentences.zh: 當時類次書目，得四萬四千四百八十六卷。

translations.literal: The classified catalogue of that time came to 44,486 juan.
translations.idiomatic: The classified catalogue of that time reached 44,486 juan.

sentences.zh: 至寧宗時續書目，又得一萬四千九百四十三卷，視《崇文總目》，又有加焉。

translations.literal: When the catalogue was continued under Emperor Ningzong, another 14,943 juan were added—an increase over the 《Comprehensive Catalogue of the Chongwen Court》.
translations.idiomatic: Ningzong's continuation added another 14,943 juan—beyond the Comprehensive Catalogue of the Chongwen Court.

sentences.zh: 自是而後，迄於終祚，國步艱難，軍旅之事，日不暇給，而君臣上下，未嚐頃刻不以文學為務，大而朝廷，微而草野，其所製作、講說、紀述、賦詠，動成卷帙，累而數之，有非前代之所及也。

translations.literal: From then until the dynasty's end, though the state's steps were hard and military affairs left no day free, ruler and ministers above and below never for a moment ceased to take literature as their task; whether at court or in the wilds, what they composed, lectured on, recorded, and versified readily filled juan upon juan—counted together, it surpassed what former ages had achieved.
translations.idiomatic: From then until the dynasty fell, though the realm was hard pressed and war consumed every day, court and countryside never ceased literary work; compositions, lectures, chronicles, and poems piled into volumes—taken together, beyond any earlier age.

sentences.zh: 雖其間釽裂大道，疣贅聖謨，幽怪恍惚，瑣碎支離有所不免，然而瑕瑜相形，雅鄭各趣，譬之萬派歸海，四瀆可分，繁星麗天，五緯可識，求約於博，則有要存焉。

translations.literal: Though among them tearing the great Way, excrescences on the sage's plan, obscure strangeness, and fragmented minutiae could not be avoided, yet flaw and jade stand beside each other, refined and vulgar each have their taste—like ten thousand streams returning to the sea, the four great rivers still distinguishable; like stars crowning the sky, the five planets still knowable; seeking the essential within the broad, something vital remains.
translations.idiomatic: To be sure, the corpus also holds ruptures of the great Way, excrescences on sage teaching, occult vagueness, and petty fragments—yet flaw and gem lie side by side, elegant and vulgar each keep their place; like myriad streams to the sea or stars in the sky, from abundance one can still find the essential.

sentences.zh: 宋舊史，自太祖至寧宗，為書凡四。

translations.literal: The old histories of Song, from Taizu to Ningzong, were four works in all.
translations.idiomatic: The old Song histories from Taizu to Ningzong were four separate works.

sentences.zh: 誌藝文者，前後部帙，有亡增損，互有異同。

translations.literal: Their treatises on arts and literature, in successive fascicles, had losses, additions, and mutual differences.
translations.idiomatic: Their arts-and-letters treatises, fascicle by fascicle, differed in omissions, additions, and wording.

sentences.zh: 今刪其重復，合為一誌，蓋以寧宗以後史之所未録者，仿前史分經、史、子、集四類而條列之，大凡為書九千八百十九部，十一萬九千九百七十二卷雲。

translations.literal: Now duplicates are deleted and combined into one treatise; what the histories after Ningzong did not record is listed by the four categories of classics, histories, masters, and collections as in earlier histories—in all 9,819 titles and 119,972 juan.
translations.idiomatic: Duplicates are now removed and merged into one treatise; works after Ningzong that earlier histories omitted are listed under classics, histories, masters, and collections as before—in all 9,819 titles and 119,972 juan.

sentences.zh: 經類十：一曰《易》類，二曰《書》類，三曰《詩》類，四曰《禮》類，五曰《樂》類，六曰《春秋》類，七曰《孝經》類，八曰《論語》類，九曰經解類，十曰小學類。

translations.literal: The classics comprise ten categories: first, 《Changes》; second, 《Documents》; third, 《Odes》; fourth, 《Rites》; fifth, 《Music》; sixth, 《Spring and Autumn》; seventh, 《Filial Piety》; eighth, 《Analects》; ninth, commentaries on the classics; tenth, philology.
translations.idiomatic: Classics fall into ten types: Changes, Documents, Odes, Rites, Music, Spring and Autumn, Filial Piety, Analects, exegetical works, and philology.
